The 443-foot Viking Haki Is the Newest Viking River Cruise Ship
8 photos
Photo: Viking Cruises
If you’re thinking about European travel, you shouldn’t miss the stunning river cruise experiences offered by one of the most acclaimed names in the industry, Viking Cruises. Operator of a flexible fleet of river ships, ocean ships, and expedition ships, Viking knows how to take boutique cruising to the next level.
Those passionate about Norse mythology will immediately recognize Haki as the self-proclaimed King of Sweden with a cruel fate. After defeating the Swedish army led by King Hugleik, Haki proclaimed himself King of Sweden, but his rulership was short-lived. He was killed in an act of revenge by two kinsmen of the former King, just three years later.
The legendary name of this Norse king is now also the name of the latest ship to join Viking’s fleet of river cruise ships. It was officially welcomed this week, and it will join its sister ships on several itineraries on the Rhine, Main, and Danube rivers.
Haki is 443 feet long, and its boutique cruising configuration is meant to welcome just 190 guests, attended by a 53-person crew. The Viking Longship is an award-winning design, said to combine classic Scandinavian design with innovative engineering. The spacious staterooms onboard the ships in this series are heralded as the largest suites available on European rivers , and these ships also offer the most al-fresco dining.
Viking Haki’s 95-suite configuration includes 25 standard staterooms, 22 French Balcony Staterooms, 39 Veranda Staterooms, seven Veranda Suites, and two Explorer Suites. One of the characteristics of the Viking Longship is that all staterooms features two full-size rooms with a veranda accessed from the living room, plus a French balcony in the bedroom.
Such spacious accommodation is possible mainly thanks to the ingenious asymmetric corridor layout of the Viking Longship design.
Onboard amenities include the Aquavit Terrace and Lounge, a beautiful indoor/outdoor space at the bow of the ship, specifically designed for elegant al-fresco dining. The Sun Deck offers beautiful 360-degree views and shaded seating, but also houses the ship’s solar panels and an organic herb garden.
Guests also have access to a Lounge &Bar, a restaurant, and a library. The lounge and the restaurant both have floor-to-ceiling windows and doors for expansive views. Lastly, a hybrid-engine system described as “ecologically friendly” contributes to a more comfortable, smoother onboard experience for the guests, by producing fewer vibrations.
With the delivery of the new Viking Haki, Viking is on track to complete its massive fleet expansion. By 2032, this expanded fleet will boast 114 river ships, 28 ocean ships, and 28 expedition ships. Following Viking Haki, 17 more river ships will be added to the fleet in 2028, all boasting the same innovative layout, greener propulsion, and luxury onboard services.
